name: 29303-longprompt-gptoss20b-eagle-1gpu
model: openai/gpt-oss-20b, with the one-layer Eagle3 drafter nebius/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-20b attached at one speculative token per step
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism, one vLLM engine; the drafter runs in the same engine on the same GPU.
architecture: sparse mixture-of-experts decoder with mxfp4 expert weights: 24 layers, hidden size 2880, 32 local experts with 4 active per token, 64 attention heads over 8 KV heads at head_dim 64, 131072-token native window, ~13 GB of weights.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 768 requests with a 3600 s safety cap, static seed 29303.
workload: synthetic `synthetic_text`, single turn: 8192 prompt tokens and 256 output tokens per request, min == max == mean on both, temperature 0 (greedy); the engine tokenizes the rendered prompt, so the reported prompt count lands a few tokens off 8192.
purpose: A long-document analysis assistant with draft-model acceleration, serving 256 concurrent 8K-token prompts on one GPU.
launch:
model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
# The drafter has to be a checkpoint THIS engine era can load, and most public gpt-oss Eagle3
# heads are not. `RedHatAI/gpt-oss-20b-speculator.eagle3` is speculators-format
# (`norm_before_fc: true`, an `input_norm.weight` tensor) and dies during weight load with
# `KeyError: 'input_norm.weight'` at llama_eagle3.py:249. `nebius/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-20b`
# is the native layout this loader accepts -- layers.0.* / fc / norm / lm_head / d2t / t2d,
# hidden 2880, fc [2880, 8640], max_position_embeddings 131072 with the target's yarn rope --
# and is what is pinned below. Verify any substitute by LOADING it, not by reading its card.
speculative-config: {"method": "eagle3", "model": "nebius/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-20b", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 16384
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# Pinned defaults, not tuning: these are what a real `vllm serve` resolves to on an 80GB non-A100
# card at this commit. Driving the engine in-process resolves a different pair (16384 / 1024),
# so pinning them is what keeps the two launch routes comparable.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024
